document.mutation_rule: Reverse the safe transfer order so the branch is deleted before dependent accounts move.
document.why_it_matters: Checks whether tests catch referential-integrity and ordering faults in transactional routines.
document.expected_observable_effect: Foreign-key failure, orphaned accounts, or partial transfer state.
document.original_snippet: UPDATE accounts SET br_no = p_new_branch WHERE br_no = p_old_branch; DELETE FROM branches WHERE br_no = p_old_branch;
document.mutant_snippet: DELETE FROM branches WHERE br_no = p_old_branch; UPDATE accounts SET br_no = p_new_branch WHERE br_no = p_old_branch;
document.content: Close Branch Orphan Accounts targets branch-closure routines. It deletes the source branch before transferring dependent accounts, which should trigger referential-integrity failures or leave the database in a partial state. This is useful for evaluating transaction-aware PL/SQL test suites.
